compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
observations.label: Text in view

observations.body: Israel comes from Rephidim into the Sinai wilderness and camps before the mountain.
observations.label: Camp before Sinai

observations.body: The wilderness journey stops at the mountain where Israel is addressed as a people brought to God.
observations.label: Wilderness role

payload.posture: Read Exodus 19:1–4 as its own wilderness scene before relating it to other journeys, memories, or visions.
payload.tension: Arrival at Sinai closes one stage of travel and opens a guarded encounter.
payload.title: The journey reaches Sinai
